title: 36 Hours in Mérida, Mexico
abstract: Mérida, a languid city of pastel mansions and evening promenades, is in the midst of a restoration boom, and the city’s cultural and restaurant scenes are flourishing.

title: 36 Hours in Mérida, Mexico
abstract: The city, now one of the safest in Mexico, is an architectural jewel, with one of the country’s largest historic centers outside Mexico City.

title: 36 Hours: Lake Placid, N.Y.
abstract: Over the last few decades, this two-time Winter Olympics host has been adding non-Olympic attractions.

title: 36 Hours: Lake Placid, N.Y.
abstract: Lake Placid has quietly been adding non-Olympic attractions, including farm-to-table restaurants, classier lodgings and a gleaming convention center.

title: 36 Hours: Salzburg, Austria
abstract: The Austrian city abounds with tourists, most searching for the sound of music — be it Mozart or the von Trapps — yet some of its best offerings are its Christmas markets and taverns.

title: 36 Hours: Salzburg, Austria
abstract: In winter, the city is at its most hospitable, as squares transform into bustling Christmas markets, and candlelit taverns fill with skiers refueling on Teutonic comfort food.

title: 36 Hours: Cambridge, Mass.
abstract: Even with the winter chill settling in, Cambridge, a city of bookstores, art houses and eclectic bars, is an ideal place to visit despite the cold.

title: 36 Hours: Cambridge, Mass.
abstract: This city of bookstores and coffeehouses, art-house cinemas and eclectic neighborhood bars barely skips a beat in winter.

title: 36 Hours: Trinidad
abstract: Creole culture, waterfalls and partying galore.

title: 36 Hours: Trinidad
abstract: Trinidad is a place of unspoiled beaches, Creole culture and the Caribbean’s most electrifying night life.
